Subject: Request: Redwood SLA template + credit model for HelioWorks

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — HelioWorks is excited about Redwood's throughput on batched inference. Procurement asked us to open the SLA discussion early. Can you share your standard SLA template and a sample monthly credit model?

High level asks from our side:
- Standard uptime target for hosted API (we expect a single % we can show procurement)
- Typical monthly credit calculation and any caps you apply
- How you handle latency SLOs for batched vs. non-batched requests (we run a mix)

I attached the RFP excerpt with our compliance questions for context. We're hoping to get something internal by next week so procurement can prepare redlines.

Cheers,
Arianna

Date: 2025-09-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Redwood SLA template + credit model for HelioWorks

Hi Arianna — appreciate the clear ask and the RFP. Attaching our standard SLA template (see redwood_sla_template_v1.pdf) and a short note on how we typically structure monthly credits and latency tiers. Quick clarifying questions before we propose edits:

1) Do you expect the SLA to cover both Hosted API and Dedicated capacity, or just Hosted initially?
2) Any required uptime floor in your contract practice (procurement sometimes insists on 99.95+)?
3) For latency SLOs, do you need per-route guarantees or an aggregate P95/P99 across all routes?

High-level: our hosted baseline in the template is 99.9% monthly availability with credits that scale by band (e.g., 99.9-99.5, 99.5-99.0, <99.0) and a monthly credit cap by percent of invoice. For batched jobs we usually nominate separate latency tiers and carveouts for scheduled batch windows. I'll loop in Laura for legal/pricing calibration.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Holt <marcus.holt@helioworks.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Arianna Cole <arianna@helioworks.com>
Date: 2025-09-15T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Redwood SLA template + credit model for HelioWorks

Soojin — thanks for the template. A couple of constraints from procurement & ops:
- HelioWorks standard ask is 99.95% for public API endpoints tied to customer-facing features; internal batch pipelines can accept lower (we'd accept 99.8 for batch).
- Procurement wants a predictable cap on credits — ideally no more than 15% of the monthly invoice, but they will consider higher during an initial ramp period.
- We run three priority classes: realtime (p50 < 50 ms, p95 < 120 ms), interactive batch (p95 < 400 ms), and heavy batch (no hard latency, but completion within SLA window).

Can Redwood map those classes to the template and show an example monthly remediation calculation? I've attached a short doc with our requirements.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Holt
Procurement Manager, HelioWorks

Attachment: HelioWorks-sla-requirements.pdf (PDF, 98 KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-17T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: HelioWorks SLA asks — proposed structure

Team — looping in Ben for pricing. My suggested compromise to present to HelioWorks:
- Hosted API: baseline 99.9% monthly availability (standard template), with an optional "elevated" tier at 99.95% available for accounts that opt into Reserved (Dedicated) capacity.
- Monthly credit bands (example):
  - 99.9%–99.5%: 5% of monthly invoice
  - 99.5%–99.0%: 12% of monthly invoice
  - <99.0%: 25% of monthly invoice
- Cap: For new pilots we can offer a temporary cap of 20% of invoice for first 90 days, then default to 15% thereafter.
- Latency SLOs: define per-class thresholds; credits triggered if p95 exceeds threshold for more than X minutes in aggregate per month. For batched windows we propose scheduled-carveouts and a rolling measurement to avoid single-window noise.

This structure keeps our baseline predictable, gives HelioWorks the option to pay for elevated availability via Dedicated pools, and gives procurement a ramping cap. Ben — any objections or adjustments on the percentages?

Cheers,
Laura
Senior Director, Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-19T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: HelioWorks SLA asks — proposed structure

Looks reasonable. I'll turn that into a short proposal to send to HelioWorks. Key points I'll include:
- Offer: 99.9% baseline for Hosted; 99.95% for Dedicated at a 12% price uplift (estimate).
- Credit calculation example (monthly invoice $50,000):
  - If availability is 99.6% -> falls in 99.9–99.5 band -> credit = 5% -> $2,500 credit applied to next invoice.
  - If availability <99.0% -> credit = 25% -> $12,500 (but capped to 20% for first 90 days).
- Latency: propose p95 thresholds and a credit trigger of 1% of monthly invoice per sustained violation window (max aggregated to monthly cap).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice excluded; emergency mitigations excluded with post-event review.

I'll attach a lightweight SL amendment and send to Arianna with the example numbers and a DocuSign-ready amendment.

—Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal-HelioWorks-sla-redwood-draft.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)
